### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**14** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0aef7888166501b9c6109ef602c97f793884b496` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a669e2756e4261c9bee42e4f33a36f4e710d2dce` — the merge of head `bfebc9b48ea877c3651ae630149a2cfae0cc3e21` into base `0aef7888166501b9c6109ef602c97f793884b496`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a669e2756e4261c9bee42e4f33a36f4e710d2dce && git checkout a669e2756e4261c9bee42e4f33a36f4e710d2dce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0aef7888166501b9c6109ef602c97f793884b496 bfebc9b48ea877c3651ae630149a2cfae0cc3e21 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0aef7888166501b9c6109ef602c97f793884b496 && git merge --no-ff bfebc9b48ea877c3651ae630149a2cfae0cc3e21

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0aef7888166501b9c6109ef602c97f793884b496
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ae045fe7ff7f90dd3c98cb64baee9ddc8a372e44`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-12T17:35Z by an isolated at-tier subagent of the dispatching session. Inputs: card #23013 (body and all four comments, the triage grade `6122902128`, the claim, the os-dev-report `6129156541` and the seat ACCEPT `6129205833`), PR #23080 (body, 10-file list, net diff `0a29bec6a..ae045fe7f`), the check-runs on the head, and `origin/main` git objects read for the anchors the diff cites (`isMultiValueField`, `resolveFieldPath`, the reference-integrity suite, the page ledger `_note`, the authorable-surface and api-surface baselines, `clause2-line.mjs`), plus objectui `origin/main` for the section-label resolver. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`RecordDetailsProps.sections[].count` — new optional closed object `{ field }`, `field` a bare machine name (`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`).** A widening of the section object's accept set; unknown keys under `count` are refused (one new strict site, the ledger counts regenerated `210 → 211`). **Right.**
2. **`sectionHeadingCountRefinement` — five refusals, every one gated on `count !== undefined`:** `count` beside `group`; `count` with no `label`; a label (each locale of an inline map, reported at that locale) with no `{{ count }}` hole; any other double-brace hole (another variable, or `count` with a formatter); the single-brace `{count}` / `${count}` read after the double-brace holes are stripped. All five sit inside the new key's accept set, so no stack that parsed at the merge base is refused (the early return, pinned by the "materializes nothing when omitted" and the "does NOT refuse a hole without `count`" tests). `count` is not in the group refinement's `derivedKeys`, so `count`+`group` reports once, at `count`. **Right.**
3. **`SECTION_HEADING_COUNT_HOLE` — new public const on `@objectstack/spec` (`ui` subpath).** Non-global by design; `api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` carry the row; `root.json` / `api-assembled.json` list no `ui` members, so no row is owed there. One grammar for the judge and the renderer. **Right.**
4. **A `{{ count }}` hole in a section that declares no `count` stays accepted** (pinned). This is the deliberate non-narrowing of `label`; judged under ③. **Right.**
5. **`@objectstack/lint` public surface:** `PAGE_SECTION_COUNT_NOT_MULTI_VALUE` is added to `index.ts`. `componentSectionCountRefs` / `checkSectionCountRefs` are module exports only, matching the siblings (`componentFieldRefs`, `componentSectionGroupRefs`, `checkFieldRefs` are not package exports either); `FieldRefConsequence` gains `'counted'` and is likewise not a package export (the index re-exports only `PageFieldFinding` and `PageFieldSeverity`). **Right.**
6. **`page-field-unknown` at `error` for a `counted` reference, through the shared `checkFieldRefs` core.** The severity rewrite (`skipped ? warning : error`, replacing `queried ? error : warning`) is equal on both pre-existing consequences, and the new `FIELD_REF_MISS` table keeps the two existing messages verbatim; the `fields[]` miss stays a warning (pinned by the severity-split test). **Right.**
7. **`page-section-count-not-multi-value` at `error`, judged by the spec's `isMultiValueField`.** Enforcement set: `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` (`MULTI_OPTION_TYPES`), or `select` / `radio` / `lookup` / `user` / `file` / `image` with `multiple: true` (`MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES`). The describe and changeset list every one of those but `radio`, so the claim is narrower than the enforcement — the safe direction under Prime Directive #10, and a prose nit only. **Right.**
8. **The skip set of `checkSectionCountRefs`:** a dotted path (the spec refuses it at parse), an object the stack does not define, an unresolved leaf (the existence core reports it once), and a resolved leaf with no `type` — the driver-provisioned `id`, which the object graph documents as "not answerable, ⛔ never read as absent". Consequence: `count: { field: 'id' }` passes lint silently; the changeset claim ("a *declared* field that holds one value") is still literally true, since `id` is not an authored field. **Right**, boundary named in ③.
9. **Where it gates.** `validatePageFieldBindings` is a member of the gating reference-integrity suite (`reference-integrity-suite.ts:368`) on `os validate` / `lint` / `build`, with the frozen `flow` runtime default, so no Studio/REST/MCP page write runs it — pre-existing, and recorded as deliberate in the suite. The shape half reaches authors as `component-props-invalid` at `warning` (`validateComponentProps`, `tier: 'advisory'`, `CLI_ONLY`). Triage's "a heading naming a field the object does not declare is refused at publish" holds at `error` for the reference half; the shape half is as strong as the props door is today, declared in Acceptance note 1 with its carrier (#23026, below). **Right.**
10. **Generated artifacts.** `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx` (two rows), the strictness-ledger counts, `api-surface/ui.json`, `export-origins/ui.json` — all four regenerated; `check:generated`, `check:api-surface` (`Type Check · consumer gates`), `check:authorable-surface` and `check:strictness-ledger` (Lint jobs) are green on the head. `authorable-surface/ui.json` has a bare `ui/RecordDetailsProps:sections` row and no section-level sub-rows (no `headerColor` row exists), so no row is owed for `count`. **Right.**
11. **Liveness: no `liveness/page.json` row, the describe carries `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]` instead.** The ledger's own `_note` says the walk drills one level and `page/regions` is RECORDED undrilled, so no `ComponentPropsMap` key has a row; `check-liveness.mts` names the describe marker as its second classification source; the in-file #20694 (`keyboardNavigation`) record is the precedent, marker dropped when the renderer landed at the pin. The dispatch's `page.json` row assumption was falsified correctly. **Right.**
12. **The i18n leg.** `ObjectTranslationDataSchema._sections.NAME.label` stores the hole verbatim (pinned); objectui `origin/main` resolves the heading through `sectionLabel → resolve → t(key, { defaultValue: '' })` and falls back to the authored label via `pickLocalized`, so on both routes the hole renders literally until the renderer fills it — exactly what the marker says. The `skipOnVariables` reading on i18next 26.4.0 is the dev's measurement (objectui pins `^26.4.0`); it is not re-measured here and the renderer half owes its own pin. **Right** as to the spec contract.
13. **Dialect.** The hole is ADR-0032 §3's kept `{{ }}` delimiter, one closed variable, no formatter; single-brace spellings are refused by name. No new dialect, no ADR amended, no governed path in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). **Right.**
14. **Prime Directive #12.** No consumer alias or `??` fallback: the lint pass yielding nothing on a non-object `count` is not tolerance of off-spec input — the shape is the props door's finding. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23013-section-heading-count.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: minor`, body line `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Both packages publish something new (a key and an export; a rule id and an export), so `minor` is the floor `yes` demands and the ceiling the diff reaches. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed (`check:adr-0087-registration` green). `skip-changeset` does not apply. **Matches.**
- The PR body and the claim spell `Clause-②: yes (widening: a new accepted key)`; `readArmToken` (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) reads the arm `widening` there (a colon after the arm is neither a word character nor `|`), and `Check Changeset` ran green twice on this head. **Clause-②: yes (widening) — carried and matching.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (os-dev-report): refuse a `{{ count }}` hole in a section with no `count`?** Answer **A — keep it accepted**, as the dev recommends and the seat answered. B is a narrowing of `label`'s accept set — BREAKING with an ADR-0087 disposition — which this card's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` does not carry; C adds a gate. Measured on `origin/main`: no section label in `examples/`, `packages/platform-objects/`, `templates/` or `apps/` carries a double-brace hole, and the only `{{count}}` spellings at `main` are the operation-message i18n sentences. If the renderer half meets a real author writing the hole without the key, a lint advisory can follow under its own card in a later minor. **Answered.**
- **Marker obligation.** `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]` drops in the change that lands objectui#12192 at the `.objectui-sha` pin. Carrier: objectui#12192 (`pm:blocked` on this card). **Escalated to its carrier, nothing owed here.**
- **Parse half advisory (Acceptance note 1 / out-of-scope 1).** The blockers the props-gate header names (#5728, #5068) both read `closed`; the error upgrade's carrier is #23026 (open, claimed by `domain:spec#3`), and the seat's pointer `6129214439` on it already names this PR's refusal set for that inventory. **Answered: dedupe to #23026, no new card.**
- **Runtime page-write door does not run the page pass (Acceptance note 2 / out-of-scope 2).** Pre-existing for `fields[]` and `group`, recorded as deliberate in the suite (`flow` default; the per-write snapshot carries no `stack.pages`). Not a defect this PR introduces or widens. **Answered: noted, not filed — Prime Directive #10's "note everything else" arm.**
- **Driver `id` passes the multi-value check silently (① item 8).** An observation, not an action: the graph's own contract forbids reading an absent `type` as single-valued. **Noted.**
- **`radio` omitted from the prose type list (① item 7).** Claim narrower than enforcement; a one-word describe/changeset nit for a later touch. **Noted.**
- **Three gates NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`).** Answered by CI on the head: `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Build Core` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are all green. **Answered.**
- **Narrowed cli consumer run; `origin/main` has moved since the merge at `0a29bec6a` (now past `275ad4229`).** CI's merge-ref run and the queue re-test cover both; information, not a contract item. **Answered.**
- **cloud#2784 NOT MEASURED (no access).** The shape is generic by construction and cloud consumes it after its v18 move (cloud#2709); no bearing on the spec half. **Answered.**
- **Lock contention, commit-trailer form, zero label writes:** process notes with no contract bearing. **Answered.**
- **Check-runs on `ae045fe7f` as read in this act:** 28 `success` (among them `Check Changeset` ×2, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` job but one), 8 `skipped` (opt-in and path-filtered gates), 7 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1–6, `Type Check · workspace`), 0 failures. The verdict below is about the contract; the seat reads convergence separately and lands nothing before it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23013-section-heading-count`
Reviewed-by: `session_01GZSPSQ5ArPjSJdxxuqwGoZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Regen-provenance: 6129375882 · `ae045fe7ff7f90dd3c98cb64baee9ddc8a372e44` → `bfebc9b48ea877c3651ae630149a2cfae0cc3e21` · per-file net diff, each head against its own merge base with `origin/main`, compared → (empty) on every source file

`domain:spec` seat 2 · session `session_01GZSPSQ5ArPjSJdxxuqwGoZ` · 2026-10-12T18:57Z. The serial-relay hop recorded on #23013 (`6129636501`).

- **The hop's commits:** `25fb63711` merges `origin/main` at `62ce45d14` (PR #23076 and PR #23079 landed). `bfebc9b48` then regenerates the generated artifacts on the merged tree.

  - Merge bases: `ae045fe7f` → `0a29bec6a`, and `bfebc9b48` → `62ce45d14`.
  - The ten files' net hunks are byte-identical between the two heads, for all nine source and generated files.
